Scmut 2026-11-16 Chapter 1 Overview We established a systematic benchmarking framework to evaluate 11 variant callers across 29 tumor samples comprising 86,531 cells from 10x Genomics and Smart-seq2 datasets. Using matched whole-exome sequencing (WES) data as reference, we assessed variant calling performance at different analysis resolutions, complemented by in silico simulations and multi-caller consensus analyses to investigate factors influencing detection accuracy and potential strategies for improving performance. This documentation provides a reproducible guide to the benchmarking workflow, including software versions, tool-specific configurations, variant calling and filtering procedures, performance evaluation, simulation protocols, and consensus-based analyses. Chapter 5 Caller consensus Caller consensus analysis was performed to evaluate whether combining variant calls from multiple tools improves variant calling performance. For each sample, variants were represented by normalized CHROM:POS:REF:ALT keys, and the number of supporting callers was counted. Combinations of two, three, and four callers were evaluated using different support thresholds, including the union (≥1 caller), intermediate consensus (≥2 or ≥3 callers), and intersection (supported by all callers). Each consensus call set was compared against the matched WES reference using RTG vcfeval within predefined callable regions to assess precision, recall, and F1-score.
